newsitem.title: USA: CME FEEDER CATTLE LIMIT DOWN AS CORN PRICES SOAR.
newsitem.headline: CME FEEDER CATTLE LIMIT DOWN AS CORN PRICES SOAR.

text.p: The limit advance in corn futures after the August crop production report pressured CME feeder cattle futures for limit losses of 1.500 cents per lb at midsession, traders said.
At 1055 CDT, feeder cattle were down the 1.500 cent limit to off 0.900 cents with September limit down at 78.975 cents. August was off 1.100 at 79.700 cents.
Live cattle futures were off 0.450 to up 0.025 with October off most at 69.400 and August off 0.025 at 65.625.
Feeders tumbled from the start following Tuesday morning's USDA crop production estimates for corn which at 9.276 million bushels, indicated much less corn than expected.
"This is strictly a corn-driven break," one trader said.
Back months of live cattle futures were also down on the corn jump but spot August found support on expectations cash fed cattle prices may work higher, traders said.
The boxed beef market may be bottoming which has prompted ideas cattle prices could firm, some traders said.
Talk that packers were showing increased interest Tuesday morning at some feedlots and demanding of delivery certificates added to early strength in spot futures, they said.
Deferred months also showed support at times on expectations of tighter fed cattle supplies in coming months.
Some estimates on Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report pointed to placements starting to fall below year ago levels.

Early placement estimates for the major seven states were ranging from 96 to 105 percent of a year ago. On-feed estimates thus far were estimated between 115 to 117 percent and marketings 103 to 107 percent of a year ago.
R.J. O'Brien bought August live cattle while RBH and Rosenthal Collins sold, traders said. Rosenthal also sold October, pit sources said.
